title: Fixed points for a multiplicative-group action lift across square-zero extensions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Put $\mathbf G_{m,R}=\operatorname{Spec}R[z,z^{-1}]$ with multiplication of units [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}C$ be an affine $R$-scheme smooth over $R$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Give $X$ an $R$-action of $\mathbf G_{m,R}$, meaning an $R$-morphism $a:\mathbf G_{m,R}\times_R X\to X$ satisfying $a(1,x)=x$ and $a(t,a(u,x))=a(tu,x)$ on all commutative $R$-algebras. For an $R$-algebra $B$ write $X(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(C,B)$; a point $x\in X(B)$ is fixed if $a(t,x_{B'})=x_{B'}$ for every commutative $B$-algebra $B'$ and every $t\in(B')^\times$. Let $p:B_1\twoheadrightarrow B_0$ be a surjective map of commutative $R$-algebras with kernel $J$ satisfying $J^2=0$. For every fixed point $x_0\in X(B_0)$ there is a fixed point $x_1\in X(B_1)$ whose image under $X(p)$ is $x_0$. No reductivity, connectedness, field, Noetherian, or residue-characteristic assumption is imposed on the base or on $X$.

source.place: Agent relative infinitesimal extension of Theorem 13.1, printed p.254, and the weight-splitting method in Lemma 13.6, printed p.256. The book states the field case; the square-zero lifting assertion over arbitrary base rings is agent-written, with its graded conormal argument recorded in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-gm-affine-action-grading] to the given action: $C=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}C_n$ as $R$-modules, $R$ maps to $C_0$, and homogeneous evaluation is $a_B(t,x)(c_n)=t^nx(c_n)$.

Write $g:C\to B_0$ for $x_0$. For $c_n\in C_n$ with $n\ne0$, test fixedness after $B_0\to B_0[z,z^{-1}]$ at the universal unit $z$. Step 1 gives $z^ng(c_n)=g(c_n)$; uniqueness of Laurent coefficients gives $g(c_n)=0$. Conversely, a map killing every $C_n$ for $n\ne0$ is fixed on every algebra extension by the formula in step 1 and finite additivity.

source.place: Tag 0EKJ, example-Gm-on-affine: homogeneous action formula, applied to the universal Laurent unit

proof.text: The surjection $p$ identifies $B_0$ with $B_1/J$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], $\operatorname{Spec}p$ is a first order thickening of affine $R$-schemes: its defining ideal on the affine target is $J$, with $J^2=0$. The affine lifting property in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] gives a lift $\operatorname{Spec}B_1\to X$ of $x_0$. The affine correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] writes it as an $R$-algebra map $f:C\to B_1$ with $pf=g$. In particular $f(C_n)\subseteq J$ for $n\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 02H0, definition-formally-smooth; application to Spec(B_1/J) inside Spec(B_1)

proof.text: For $c=\sum_n c_n$ set $h(c)=f(c_0)$. The direct-sum decomposition makes $h$ additive and $R$-linear, and $h(1)=1$. Check multiplication on $a\in C_m$, $b\in C_n$. If $m=n=0$, the assertion follows from multiplicativity of $f$. If $m+n\ne0$, then $h(ab)=0$ and at least one of $h(a),h(b)$ is zero. If $m+n=0$ with $m\ne0$, then $h(ab)=f(ab)=f(a)f(b)=0$, since both factors lie in $J$ and $J^2=0$, while $h(a)h(b)=0$. Finite distributivity proves $h(cd)=h(c)h(d)$ for arbitrary $c,d$. Thus $h$ is an $R$-algebra map.

source.place: Agent square-zero argument using the weight-splitting idea of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256; the book proves the field case, not this relative assertion

proof.text: For every $c=\sum_n c_n$, $ph(c)=g(c_0)=g(c)$ by step 2. Also $h$ kills each $C_n$ with $n\ne0$, so the converse in step 2 proves fixedness after every $B_1$-algebra extension. Hence $h$ defines the required fixed lift $x_1$.
